diseases.name: Newcastle Disease (NCD)
diseases.transmission: Highly contagious; spreads via droppings, contaminated feed/water, air, and equipment
first_response: Restrict movement of birds, people, and equipment on/off farm
Contact a vet or livestock officer immediately
diseases.prevention: Vaccination (day-old and booster schedule), strict biosecurity

diseases.name: Coccidiosis
diseases.transmission: Ingestion of oocysts from contaminated litter, feed, or water; thrives in wet/dirty bedding
first_response: Administer anticoccidial medication (e.g., amprolium) via water
diseases.prevention: Coccidiostats in feed, dry litter management, avoid overcrowding

diseases.name: Fowl Typhoid
diseases.transmission: Contaminated feed/water, egg transmission, carrier birds
first_response: Cull chronically infected carrier birds where advised
diseases.prevention: Biosecurity, sourcing chicks from certified hatcheries, vaccination where available

diseases.name: Infectious Bursal Disease (Gumboro / IBD)
symptoms: Birds pecking at their own vent
Sudden mortality in young birds (3-6 weeks)
diseases.transmission: Highly contagious via droppings, contaminated equipment, indirect contact
first_response: Provide supportive care (electrolytes, vitamins in water)
Contact vet — no specific cure, focus on secondary infection prevention
diseases.prevention: Vaccination at recommended age, strict biosecurity

diseases.name: Fowl Pox
symptoms: Wart-like lesions on comb, wattles, face (dry form)
Reduced feed intake, drop in egg production
Generally lower mortality unless wet form affects breathing
diseases.transmission: Mosquito bites, direct contact, contaminated equipment
first_response: Apply mild antiseptic to skin lesions

diseases.name: Chronic Respiratory Disease (CRD) / Mycoplasmosis
diseases.transmission: Direct contact, airborne, egg transmission, stress-triggered flare-ups
first_response: Improve ventilation and reduce stocking density
diseases.prevention: Good ventilation, stress reduction, sourcing from CRD-free flocks

diseases.name: Infectious Coryza
diseases.transmission: Direct contact, contaminated water/feed, airborne over short distances
diseases.prevention: Biosecurity, avoiding mixing ages/flocks, vaccination in high-risk areas

diseases.name: Heat Stress (non-infectious)
symptoms: Panting, wings held away from body
Reduced feed intake, increased water intake
Lethargy, sudden deaths in severe heat
first_response: Ensure constant access to cool water
Feed during cooler parts of the day
diseases.prevention: Proper housing ventilation design, adequate water access, shade structures
